comment: Solid teacher, discussions are opinionated in class and although she is clearly left-wing allows room for students to dissent. Allows rewrites for papers and homework is graded on completion  & are tri-weekly couple sentence journal entries that you can reflect on your readings with.

Professor Boxer is very fair with grading and allows rewrites which is great. She definitely has strong opinions about certain topics but tries to acknowledge opposing points. She urges everyone to participate in discussions and it can really help your grade along with turning in weekly journals on time. Best not to choose broad topics for papers.

Prof Boxer is very nice and caring, but the lectures are extremely dense and not enough discussions. I think just reading the articles would be similar to going to class, and the grading is sometimes unclear. While she does care about her students, her office hours are not too helpful so you might have to teach yourself some material.

Having very limited prior experience with Philosophy, I found this course to be difficult. The material was interesting but I found the essays to be very challenging to write. She allowed for essay rewrites though! Dr. Boxer presented the material in a good format. It was sometimes hard to communicate with her outside of class (email/office hours)

I do not agree with the other reviews of this professor; maybe she changed the format of the class upon reading reviews because discussion is fair and balanced. The course material is pretty interesting, ranging from permissibility of abortion to organ donation. Important to keep in mind this is a philosophy course so the readings can be very dense

I would have gained the same amount of knowledge on bioethics from simply reading the articles and then watching a right wing and a left wing robot whine about their opinion. It is an overall shame that such riveting and powerful material be wasted in a class taught by someone who doesn't care. She makes no effort to encourage discussion. Bummer

Sitting through this class is like watching grass grow. Paper grading criteria is very ambiguous, and her lectures are repetitive and un-engaging. As far as the class goes, it is so obvious her ideals lean strongly liberal that it is almost impossible to take a different stance on the issues she brings up.
